AgentRef.description: Who made a change; for software agents, which model (SUB-24).
AgentRef.title: AgentRef

AmbiguityKeepEnum.description: What the analyst asks of ambiguous cuts (CAP-22): keep the bearing to port or to starboard of the host track's course at each cut's time, as legacy Debrief's Keep port bearing and Keep starboard bearing decide it (by the side of the bearing recorded first); keep the bearing recorded first, or its ambiguous twin, as the analyst clicked it on the map; or make the cuts ambiguous again.
AmbiguityKeepEnum.title: AmbiguityKeepEnum

AmbiguityResolution.description: Ambiguous cuts resolved, or made ambiguous again, as the map, a menu or an agent asks (CAP-22): one recorded, undoable step (product owner, 24 Oct 2026). The cuts are those named, or else the cuts of the sensors named within a period (the time window, as the analyst sets it). Cuts with no ambiguous bearing are left as they are, and the step says how many.

cut_ids.description: The cuts to resolve, by feature id. Or give sensor_ids, and perhaps a period.

period.description: The cuts whose times fall in it, ends included, of the sensors named.

sensor_ids.description: Sensors whose cuts in the period are resolved; every cut of each, without a period.

AmbiguityResolution.title: AmbiguityResolution

AngleUnitEnum.description: Units an angle may be stored in (UCUM codes).
AngleUnitEnum.title: AngleUnitEnum

AngularRateUnitEnum.description: Units an angular rate may be stored in (UCUM codes). Degrees per minute is the analysts' standard for bearing rate.
AngularRateUnitEnum.title: AngularRateUnitEnum

AnnotationAppearance.description: How an annotation is drawn: its line, its fill and its label. Data colours do not change with the theme (DEV-07). Widths and sizes are in screen pixels, so they are the same at every zoom.

colour.description: Its line's colour, and a label's or a marker's dot. Lower-case hex RGB, for example "#c7820a". Label text is drawn in the theme's text colour, so it stays readable on any map.

fill_colour.description: Colour inside an area, circle or ellipse. Lower-case hex RGB. Left out, the line's colour.

fill_opacity.description: How opaque the fill of an area, circle or ellipse is, from 0 (none) to 1 (solid). Left out, 0.25 with a fill colour, or else a faint tint of 0.05, so what lies inside stays clear.

label_size.description: Height of its label's text in screen pixels.

line_width.description: Width of its line in screen pixels.

AnnotationAppearance.title: AnnotationAppearance

AnnotationFeature.description: Shapes, labels and chart furniture as ordinary GeoJSON (CAP-03). An annotation with only a time has null geometry and shall give a time or a time range (CAP-04); chart furniture has null geometry and needs neither. A circle or an ellipse is a polygon approximating it, for other tools, with its centre and size as properties, which Debrief draws from.
AnnotationFeature.title: AnnotationFeature

appearance.description: How it is drawn on the map. Left out, or any member of it left out, means Debrief's default for annotations. Content, like a track's colour: changing it is a recorded, undoable change (SUB-22).

items.description: The centre of a circle or an ellipse, [longitude, latitude] in WGS84 degrees. Its geometry is the polygon that approximates it.

furniture.description: What chart furniture it is. Chart furniture has no geometry and needs no time.

hidden.description: Not drawn on the map. Still listed, and still selectable, in the outline. Content: hiding is a recorded, undoable change (SUB-22).

orientation.description: The direction of an ellipse's longer axis from its centre, true north, clockwise.

radius.description: A circle's radius, along geodesics from its centre.

semi_major.description: Half an ellipse's longer axis, along the geodesic from its centre.

semi_minor.description: Half an ellipse's shorter axis, along the geodesic from its centre.

shape.description: How it is drawn. Required for circles and ellipses; otherwise it may be left out and follows from the geometry.

AnnotationShapeEnum.description: How an annotation is drawn (CAP-03). Left out, it follows from the geometry: a line string is a line, a polygon an area, a point a label (style label) or a marker, and no geometry a note. Circles and ellipses must say so, since GeoJSON has no curves: their geometry is a polygon that approximates them, for other tools, and their own properties (centre, radius or semi-axes and orientation) say exactly what they are.
AnnotationShapeEnum.title: AnnotationShapeEnum

AnnotationSpec.description: An annotation as the analyst describes it in a form, or an agent in a request: what is made into an annotation feature, recorded as one step in the plot's history (CAP-03, SUB-19). Positions are numbers here; forms read them in the analyst's notation and say what they mean.

items.description: [longitude, latitude] pairs: the line's positions, or the area's corners (not closed); one, the centre or position, for a circle, ellipse, label or marker; none for a note.

AnnotationSpec.title: AnnotationSpec

ArrayModeEnum.description: How a towed array's position follows the ship (CAP-22; product owner, 24 Oct 2026), legacy Debrief's array centre modes.
ArrayModeEnum.title: ArrayModeEnum

AssetKindEnum.description: What an asset holds in Debrief terms.
AssetKindEnum.title: AssetKindEnum

ChartFurnitureEnum.description: Chart furniture a plot can carry (CAP-03). The scale bar is always drawn.
ChartFurnitureEnum.title: ChartFurnitureEnum

CollationView.description: The analyst's answers to collation's marks, each for one revision of an item, so a later revision is marked again.

dismissed.description: Items marked as new data for this plot that the analyst set aside (Not now), at the revision then (CAP-10).

reviewed.description: Revised items this plot drew from that the analyst reviewed it against, clearing its review flag, at the revision reviewed (CAP-12).

CollationView.title: CollationView

ContextTracksEnum.description: How the map draws each track outside the time window: its context (CAP-29). An analyst's setting for the minimum contrast can show faint as visible, never hidden as anything else.
ContextTracksEnum.title: ContextTracksEnum

CoverageItem.description: A catalogue item in the folder tree the plot draws from.

new_data.description: Marked as new data for the plot (CAP-10).

revised.description: The plot took data from this item at a revision it no longer has (CAP-12).

CoverageItem.title: CoverageItem

CoverageItemRoleEnum.description: What an item is to the plot.
CoverageItemRoleEnum.title: CoverageItemRoleEnum

CoverageLinkEnum.description: How a source's track is known to be the plot's platform.
CoverageLinkEnum.title: CoverageLinkEnum

CoveragePeriod.description: A period in which the same sources have data for a platform.

chosen.description: The source supplying the period; left out where the plot has none of its data yet.

sources.description: The platform's sources with data throughout the period, by their place in its list.

CoveragePeriod.title: CoveragePeriod

CoveragePlatform.description: One of the plot's tracks, and every source of data for its platform.

periods.description: The track's time cut where the sources with data change, in time order: each with the sources that have data then and the one that supplies it.

sources.description: The plot's own data first, then items' tracks linked or proposed.

track.description: The track's feature id in the plot.

CoveragePlatform.title: CoveragePlatform

CoverageReport.description: Coverage for one plot (CAP-08, CAP-09): its platforms with every source of data for each, the items in the folder tree it draws from with their marks, and whether the plot itself may need review.

catalogue.description: The plot's catalogue, by its own id.

end.description: The latest time any source shown has data.

note.description: Anything the analyst should know about what is shown.

review.description: The plot drew from items since revised, so it may need review (CAP-12).

start.description: The earliest time any source shown has data.

CoverageReport.title: CoverageReport

CoverageSource.description: A track in a catalogue item with data for the platform.

name.description: The track's name in that item.

revised.description: The plot took data from this item at a revision it no longer has.

CoverageSource.title: CoverageSource

DebriefFeatureCollection.description: The unit of analysis (SUB-05), stored as an asset of a STAC item.

history.description: The plot's whole history: every step, with its provenance and whether it is applied, undone or abandoned, and the current step (SUB-19, SUB-21, decision 13 Oct). A GeoJSON foreign member, so other tools still read the file as GeoJSON. Not content: left out of every content hash. Last in the file. A plot sent to a view or a tool never carries it.

DebriefFeatureCollection.title: DebriefFeatureCollection

Delta.description: One recorded change, in the earlier layout: a file of its own in the plot's history folder. Read only to move a history into its plot file.

added.description: Features added, never with the whole-plot feature's view.

after.description: The delta this one was applied on top of (0 for the first).

modified.description: Features changed, in full, replacing those with the same id.

named_sets.description: Named sets added or replaced, by id.

order.description: Feature ids in the order the plot holds them after this change.

records.description: The operation that made the change.

result_hash.description: Content hash of the plot file after this delta, island left out.

seq.description: Position in the plot's history, from 1, with no gaps.

Delta.title: Delta

DurationUnitEnum.description: Units a duration may be stored in (UCUM codes).
DurationUnitEnum.title: DurationUnitEnum

ExportLog.description: The analyst's own export log, exports.json beside their Debrief configuration: the newest 2,000 exports their plots could not keep.
ExportLog.title: ExportLog

FigureSource.description: Where an image came from: a plot in one of the analyst's catalogues, at the revision the image was exported at (Find source of image).

catalogue.description: The catalogue's own id, from its catalog.json.

copied.description: The image's plot key names another plot: this is a copy of it with the same content at that revision (a colleague's, or one moved to another catalogue).

export.description: The export log entry for the image, where the plot's log or the analyst's own has one. A footer's short form may name several exports of one revision: each is a source of its own, to choose from.

store.description: The catalogue's id in the analyst's configuration.

FigureSource.title: FigureSource

FixIntervalAllEnum.description: A track's time labels or symbols at every recorded fix (CAP-32), legacy Debrief's "All" (decision, product owner, 15 Oct 2026): still thinned when zoomed out. Not for arrows.
FixIntervalAllEnum.title: FixIntervalAllEnum

FixIntervalOffEnum.description: A track's labels, symbols or direction arrows explicitly turned off (CAP-32), rather than left to Debrief's default.
FixIntervalOffEnum.title: FixIntervalOffEnum

FixMark.description: One fix of a track marked by the analyst, or by a legacy plot: drawn in a colour of its own, labelled on the map, carrying a comment, or always showing its time label or symbol. Found by its time, not its place in the track, so a mark stays with its fix when fixes before it are removed, the track is split or merged, or it is moved, rotated, sheared, stretched or smoothed. Where two fixes share a time, the mark is the first's.

colour.description: The fix's own colour, lower-case hex RGB: its marker and the line from it to the next fix are drawn in it.

comment.description: Free text about the fix, shown when the analyst points at it and in the Timeline.

label.description: Text drawn on the map beside the fix.

show_label.description: The fix always shows its time label, as the track's label_interval draws them, whatever that interval is and at any zoom (CAP-32; decision, product owner, 15 Oct 2026: force on only, so true when given). Never drawn twice where the interval falls on the same time.

show_symbol.description: The fix always shows its symbol, as the track's symbol_interval draws them, whatever that interval is and at any zoom (CAP-32); true when given.

time.description: The time of the fix marked; one of the track's times.

FixMark.title: FixMark

time_zone.description: IANA time zone for display, or UTC for Zulu time (SUB-01).

HistoryHead.description: Where a plot's history stood, in the earlier layout (history/head.json). Read only to move a history into its plot file.

abandoned.description: Deltas undone and then superseded by a new change.

current.description: Sequence number of the last delta the plot reflects; 0 for none.

plot_hash.description: Content hash the plot file has when it reflects current, island left out.

HistoryHead.title: HistoryHead

HistoryStep.description: One recorded change to a plot, in its plot file's history.

added.description: Features added. A whole-plot feature here never carries its view: the island is not content (SUB-22).

after.description: The step this one was applied on top of (0 for the first). Replay follows these links back from a step to the first.

modified.description: Features changed, in full, replacing those with the same id.

named_sets.description: Named sets added or replaced, by id.

order.description: Feature ids in the order the plot holds them after this change, when that is not the natural order (features kept in place, added ones last).

records.description: The operation that made the change. Usually one; a baseline step, taken when a plot made outside Debrief is first opened, carries all the plot's earlier records.

result_hash.description: Hash of the plot's content after this step: the plot file with its island and its history left out, as Debrief writes it (SUB-22).

seq.description: Position in the plot's history, from 1, with no gaps.

state.description: Applied, undone or abandoned: what the after links and the history's current step say. Not part of step_hash, since undo changes it.

step_hash.description: SHA-256 of this step's canonical JSON, without step_hash and state, followed by the previous step's step_hash (see the module description).

HistoryStep.title: HistoryStep

ImageExport.description: One image exported from a plot, as the plot's export log records it in its island: view state, never a step (decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026). What the analyst exported, so the image can be traced and its view shown again.

by.description: Who exported it: the agent's name.

file.description: The file's name, without its folder.

footer.description: Whether the image shows its ID in a footer.

revision.description: The plot's revision exported (its content hash): the step it was exported at.

time.description: Current time and the time window when it was exported.

tote.description: Which tracks the Tote compared when it was exported, so the plot traced from the image shows the Tote, and its lines on the map, as the figure did (decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026).

viewport.description: The area of the map exported.

ImageExport.title: ImageExport

ImageFormatEnum.description: How an image is written (decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026; no JPEG).
ImageFormatEnum.title: ImageFormatEnum

ImagePresetEnum.description: The size an image is drawn at.
ImagePresetEnum.title: ImagePresetEnum

ImageRequest.description: What the host asks the map to draw for an export (export_image).

footer_text.description: The image's ID in its short form, to draw in a corner; left out for no footer.

ImageRequest.title: ImageRequest

ImageThemeEnum.description: The colours an image is drawn in.
ImageThemeEnum.title: ImageThemeEnum

ItemRef.description: A catalogue item an operation took data from, at one revision (CAP-09 to CAP-12). Items are named by their catalogue's own id (the catalog.json id, not the analyst's name for the folder) and their item id, so the reference means the same on every analyst's machine.

catalogue.description: The id in the item's catalog.json.

item.description: The item's id in that catalogue.

revision.description: The item's revision when it was read: the content hash of its plot (its whole-plot details included), so any recorded change to the item, of data or details, is a new revision.

title.description: The item's title when it was read, to name it if it has gone.

ItemRef.title: ItemRef

ItemRevision.description: One revision of a catalogue item; for an answer the analyst gave (Not now, Reviewed), who gave it and when, a light audit trail kept in the island (decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026).

by.description: Who gave the answer: the agent's name.

ItemRevision.title: ItemRevision

id.description: Unique within this file; stable when the store is renamed.

location.description: Absolute path to the folder holding catalog.json: a POSIX path, a Windows drive path or a UNC share.

read_only.description: When true, Debrief offers no action that would write to the store. A courtesy, not access control: filesystem permissions decide that (SEC-01).

LabelPositionEnum.description: Where an annotation's label is drawn, relative to it.
LabelPositionEnum.title: LabelPositionEnum

LengthUnitEnum.description: Units a length may be stored in (UCUM codes).
LengthUnitEnum.title: LengthUnitEnum

LineStyleEnum.description: How an annotation's line is drawn.
LineStyleEnum.title: LineStyleEnum

LoggedExport.description: An export recorded in the analyst's own export log, beside their Debrief configuration, where the plot's could not be written (a read-only catalogue, say), so every export stays traceable (decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026).

catalogue.description: The catalogue's own id, from its catalog.json.

LoggedExport.title: LoggedExport

MeasureDefinition.description: One measure the Tote can show. The core measures are Debrief's own; a study may add more (CAP-07), each worked out in Python.

explanation.description: How it is worked out, in a sentence.

id.description: Unique among measures, such as range or relative_bearing.

label.description: Its row heading in the Tote, before the unit, short enough for a narrow view.

title.description: Its name in full, for hover text and screen readers.

MeasureDefinition.title: MeasureDefinition

MeasureDisplayEnum.description: How a measure's value is written for people, by the formatting service (SUB-04).
MeasureDisplayEnum.title: MeasureDisplayEnum

MeasureGroup.description: A named, reusable set of measures tied to a mode of analysis (CAP-07), shown by the Tote in this order. Every group extends the shared core: extends names the group it adds to (core itself extends nothing). A study's own groups will be defined by its lead analyst and kept in the study catalogue, shared by every plot in the study.

extends.description: The group whose measures come first, before this one's own; left out for core.

measures.description: The ids of the measures shown, in order, those of the group it extends included.

MeasureGroup.title: MeasureGroup

MeasureValue.description: One measure's value at current time; value left out where it cannot be worked out (no depth recorded, say).

unit.description: The UCUM unit of value, such as m, deg or m/s; formatted for people by the views (SUB-04).

MeasureValue.title: MeasureValue

NarrativeFeature.description: One narrative entry (CAP-19, CAP-20, EXT-14): what a platform, a person or a document logged at a time. A feature of its own with null geometry, as a time-only annotation is, so other GeoJSON tools read it, and each entry added, changed or deleted is one small recorded, undoable step (SUB-19). Every narrative feature in a plot together makes the plot's narrative: one combined Zulu time axis, however many sources it came from, in the order narrative_order gives (time; then source, ignoring case; then the plot's order, so a log's own order at one time is kept).
NarrativeFeature.title: NarrativeFeature

NarrativeImportAnswers.description: What the analyst answered for documents of one dialect: the types not read (so a type not seen before is read), whether only entries within the plot's period, and the track each platform was said to be.

dialect.description: The dialect, such as narrative-document or rider-narrative.

skip_types.description: Entry types the analyst chose not to read; "" for entries with no type.

tracks.description: The track the analyst said each platform is, by the track's name.

within_period.description: Only the entries within the plot's tracks' period.

NarrativeImportAnswers.title: NarrativeImportAnswers

entry_type.description: What kind of entry, in the source's own words, such as legacy Debrief's GenComment, Posn, CSD or FCS. Free text: each source has its own types. Left out where the source gives none.

source.description: Who wrote it: the platform, person or document whose log it is (legacy Debrief's track name on an entry), such as "BLUE ONE".

text.description: What was logged. May run to several lines.

time.description: When it was logged, to the millisecond, Zulu (SUB-01).

track_id.description: The track the entry belongs to, where one is known: by default the track named as its source. A track since deleted leaves the link, which is then ignored.

NarrativeSpec.description: A narrative entry as the analyst describes it in a form, or an agent in a request (debrief/add_narrative, debrief/edit_narrative): made into a narrative feature as one recorded step (CAP-20).
NarrativeSpec.title: NarrativeSpec

NewDataMark.description: Why an item is marked as new data for a plot (CAP-10): it came in after the plot, through Debrief's import, within the folder tree the plot draws from, and has data for the plot's platforms or within its period; the plot has not taken it or set it aside at this revision.

note.description: What the mark says, for its tooltip and screen readers.

platforms.description: The plot's tracks it has data for.

within_period.description: It has data within the plot's period.

NewDataMark.title: NewDataMark

NonSpatialResult.description: A number, table or graph (TL-13), held column by column. A number is one column with one value; a graph plots its first column against the rest.
NonSpatialResult.title: NonSpatialResult

ObservationTypeEnum.description: Sensor observation types Debrief imports (CAP-22). Frequency is never imported.
ObservationTypeEnum.title: ObservationTypeEnum

explanation.description: Shown beside the field on the form (CAP-24).

minimum.description: Lower bound for number, integer and quantity kinds; for a quantity, in the default's unit.

ParameterKindEnum.description: Parameter kinds Debrief can build a form for (TL-07).
ParameterKindEnum.title: ParameterKindEnum

ParameterValue.description: A tool parameter value as supplied or recorded (TL-07, SUB-19). Scalars, or a quantity with its unit.
ParameterValue.title: ParameterValue

unit.description: UCUM unit code, required when quantity_kind is given.

PayloadRef.description: Envelope for data LinkML expresses badly (CON-02): the payload's format, a versioned reference to its inner schema, units, CRS and time reference.

crs.description: Coordinate reference system of any positions in the payload.

href.description: Path relative to the referencing file.

time_reference.description: Time scale of any times in the payload. Always UTC (SUB-01).

PayloadRef.title: PayloadRef

PlatformTrack.description: A platform, as a document names it, and the track it was said to be.

track.description: The track's name; left out, the platform belongs to no track.

PlatformTrack.title: PlatformTrack

PlotFeature.description: The whole plot: its own details, and its view (the island). At most one per plot. Geometry is always null, so the plot file stays plain GeoJSON for other tools.
PlotFeature.title: PlotFeature

PlotHistory.description: A plot's whole history, kept in its plot file as the top-level member history (decision 13 Oct). Steps are numbered from 1 with no gaps, in the order they were made.

current.description: The step the plot's content reflects; 0 for none (an empty plot). Never an abandoned step.

head_hash.description: The last step's step_hash, or the starting value for a history with no steps, so a step removed from the end is noticed.

PlotHistory.title: PlotHistory

description.description: What the plot is for. Content.

title.description: The plot's title. Content, like everything outside view.

view.description: The island: how the plot is being viewed. Outside the plot's history (see the module description). Kept last, so it is easy to find and strip.

PlotView.description: View state saved in the plot file: not content, so not undoable and not recorded in provenance (SUB-22). Two people changing it at once are told, not silently overwritten (SUB-28). Later view state joins here.

collation.description: What the analyst has said of catalogue items while collating (CAP-10, CAP-12): new data set aside for now, and revisions reviewed. View state: never a step in the history.

context_tracks.description: How tracks outside the time window are drawn (CAP-29). Left out means visible.

exports.description: The plot's export log: each image exported from it, with its ID, the revision exported, when, by whom, the view and the time, the format and the file's name (SUB-25; decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026). View state: never a step, so an export changes neither the plot's revision nor any product that drew from it.

narrative_on_map.description: Whether the map shows the narrative entry current time is at in a small box beside its track, for ten minutes of plot time; left out means it does. Turned off and on in the Timeline. View state, like the Tote's lines: never a step in the history (decision, product owner, 15 Oct 2026).

time_window.description: The plot's time window: the period shown, one for the whole plot (CAP-28, CAP-29). Start shall not be after end.

tote.description: Which tracks the Tote compares, and through which measure group (CAP-06, CAP-07). View state, like the window: changing it is never a step in the history (decision, 14 Oct 2026).

PlotView.title: PlotView

PlottingModeEnum.description: How a track is plotted, as legacy Debrief asked of each track imported (CAP-01, decision, product owner, 14 Oct 2026).
PlottingModeEnum.title: PlottingModeEnum

PolygonGeometry.description: Linear rings; the first is the exterior. Each ring is closed (first position equals last).
PolygonGeometry.title: PolygonGeometry

drawn_from.description: Catalogue items the operation took data from, each at the revision it read (CAP-09 to CAP-12): PROV's wasDerivedFrom. A product whose provenance names an item at a revision it no longer has may need review (CAP-12).

notes.description: Free-text notes such as truncations or omitted content (EXT-14, EXT-15).

parameters.description: Parameter values the operation ran with, so replay can repeat it (SUB-19).

seed.description: Random seed, for operations that use randomness (SUB-20).

selected.description: Ids of the features the operation was applied to, in selection order, so replay can repeat it (SUB-19).

QuantityKindEnum.description: Physical quantity kinds that carry units (SUB-02).
QuantityKindEnum.title: QuantityKindEnum

RenderedImage.description: The image the map drew (image_rendered), before its ID goes into its metadata.

data.description: A PNG as base 64, or an SVG as its text.

notes.description: What the image leaves out that the map shows, for the analyst: reference tiles that could not be read, say.

viewport.description: The area of the map drawn.

RenderedImage.title: RenderedImage

ResultColumn.description: One column; exactly one of numbers or strings is given.

unit.description: UCUM unit code, required when quantity_kind is given.

ResultColumn.title: ResultColumn

ReviewFlag.description: A product that drew from catalogue items since revised, so may need review (CAP-12), until the analyst clears it.

note.description: What the flag says, for its tooltip and screen readers.

revised.description: Each item revised since the product took data from it, at its revision now.

ReviewFlag.title: ReviewFlag

RevisionShown.description: The plot is shown as it was at an earlier revision, read-only: the one an image was exported at (show_plot).

figure.description: The image's ID, in its short form, when one was traced.

step.description: The step whose revision is shown.

RevisionShown.title: RevisionShown

plot.description: Href of the plot the selection belongs to.

SensorCutFeature.description: One cut of a sensor (CAP-22): a bearing from the host track at a time, perhaps with the ambiguous bearing a towed array cannot tell it from, and which of the two the analyst kept. Geometry is null: the cut is drawn from the host track's position at its time (as the map places tracks, along the geodesic between fixes), or from the position recorded with it, along the geodesic at its bearing to its range, or else past the edge of the map's view (twice the view's larger side, at most 5 degrees of arc, 300 nmi, as legacy Debrief draws it). Frequency is never imported (CAP-22, EXT-03). A bearing error is not held yet: no legacy format defines what one means (product owner, 24 Oct 2026); an optional bearing_error here is the way to add it, and wedges with it.
SensorCutFeature.title: SensorCutFeature

SensorCutKeptEnum.description: Which of an ambiguous cut's two recorded bearings the analyst kept (CAP-22): the side resolved. Recorded as the bearing kept, not as port or starboard, because which side a bearing is on depends on the host track's course at the cut's time, which a later edit of the track (a move, dead reckoning) can change; what the analyst judged is which bearing was the target's. Debrief says it as port or starboard.
SensorCutKeptEnum.title: SensorCutKeptEnum

ambiguous_bearing.description: A towed array's ambiguous bearing: the mirror image of bearing about the array, on the other side of the host's course. Left out for a cut that was never ambiguous.

bearing.description: The bearing to the target, true, clockwise from north, from 0 up to 360 degrees.

bearing_accuracy.description: The bearing accuracy a ;SENSOR3: line gives, kept exactly as written: no format says what it means (a standard deviation, a half-width), so it is not drawn (product owner, 24 Oct 2026).

colour.description: The cut's own colour, lower-case hex RGB; left out, its sensor's, as legacy Debrief lets a cut take its sensor's colour.

course.description: The course, true, the cut's port and starboard are told by, pinned with a derived origin when its track was split (the course logged where the sensor was then). Left out, the host's logged course at the cut's time. Only with origin.

hidden.description: Not drawn on the map. Content, like hiding any feature (SUB-22).

label.description: Text the source gives the cut, such as legacy Debrief's label.

items.description: [longitude, latitude] of the sensor, where the source recorded it with the cut (legacy Debrief's absolute origin): the cut is drawn from there instead of from the host track. Left out, from the host track's position at the cut's time. Where origin_derived is true, Debrief worked it out (where the sensor was, pinned when its track was split) and the source did not record it.

origin_derived.description: True where origin is not recorded by the source but derived by Debrief: where the sensor (its array astern, if it has one) was before its track was split, pinned so the cut is drawn, and its side told, as before (round 3 review, 24 Oct 2026). A TMA residual can tell a recorded origin from a derived one by it. Only with origin.

range.description: How far the target was, where the source says: the cut is drawn to that range. Left out, drawn past the edge of the view. A range of 0 (a ;SENSOR2: or ;SENSOR3: line's, as legacy read it) is drawn as a point where the cut was taken, as legacy drew it.

resolved.description: Which of the two bearings the analyst kept, for a cut with an ambiguous bearing; left out while it is unresolved, when both are drawn. Each resolution, of one cut or of every cut in a period, is one recorded, undoable step with provenance (product owner, 24 Oct 2026), and can be undone or reset to ambiguous.

sensor_id.description: The sensor the cut is from, a sensor feature in the plot.

time.description: When the cut was taken, to the millisecond, Zulu (SUB-01).

SensorFeature.description: A sensor carried by a track (CAP-22): a bow sonar, a towed array, the bearings read from a narrative. Its cuts are features of their own (SensorCutFeature), each naming it, so resolving one cut, or the cuts of a period, is one small recorded step (SUB-19), as each narrative entry is a feature of its own. Geometry is null: a cut is drawn from where the host track was at its time, so a track edited (moved, sheared, plotted by dead reckoning) carries its cuts with it, and a TMA solution (CAP-21) can be rooted in the cuts' times.
SensorFeature.title: SensorFeature

SensorObservationsFeature.description: A set of sensor observations, such as weeks of bearings, held as an opaque payload (CON-02, NFR-06). Geometry is null; positions come from the host track at each observation time.
SensorObservationsFeature.title: SensorObservationsFeature

hidden.description: Not drawn on the map. Still listed, and still selectable, in the outline. Content: hiding is a recorded, undoable change (SUB-22).

array_mode.description: How the array follows the ship: back along its past track (worm in the hole, the default, as legacy's) or straight astern (plain). Only with array_offset.

array_offset.description: How far astern of the ship the sensor is (a towed array), so its cuts are drawn, and port and starboard told, from the array's position, not the ship's (product owner, 24 Oct 2026). Left out, the sensor is at the ship. Set by the analyst as a recorded, undoable step, or read from a legacy plot (its Offset, astern).

colour.description: The colour its cuts are drawn in, lower-case hex RGB, unless a cut has its own. Content, like a track's colour: each change is a recorded, undoable step (SUB-22).

hidden.description: None of its cuts drawn on the map. Still listed, and still selectable, in the outline, under its track. Content: hiding is a recorded, undoable change (SUB-22).

host_track_id.description: The track carrying the sensor (ownship): its cuts are drawn from that track's position at each cut's time (or its array's, astern). A track split: the cuts from the split on go with the second part, as a sensor of its own (a new id) where the sensor had cuts before it too; cuts between the parts' fixes keep the position they were drawn from. Tracks merged: sensors of one name are one again, the merged track's.

legacy_symbology.description: The REP symbology code its colour came from, such as "@A", kept for export.

name.description: The sensor's name, as its source gives it, such as "Towed array" or "2087".

SharedStateChange.description: A change to some or all of shared state, as set by a view or returned by a tool (TL-10, TL-11).

save_window.description: From a tool whose purpose is to set the time window: save time's range as the plot's window. Honoured only when the analyst ran the tool by hand on this plot; otherwise, and without it, a range beyond the saved window is shown, never saved (CAP-28). Needs time.

SharedStateChange.title: SharedStateChange

SourceRef.description: An immutable source file read by an operation (SUB-10, SUB-11).
SourceRef.title: SourceRef

SourceTrackRef.description: A track in a catalogue item, as collation names it (CAP-08, CAP-09): the item by its catalogue's own id and its item id, the track by its feature id there, and its name when last read, to show if the item has gone.

catalogue.description: The id in the item's catalog.json.

track.description: The track's feature id in that item.

SourceTrackRef.title: SourceTrackRef

SpeedUnitEnum.description: Units a speed may be stored in (UCUM codes).
SpeedUnitEnum.title: SpeedUnitEnum

key.description: The asset's key in the item's assets object; not written inside the asset.
The asset's key in the item's assets object; not written inside the asset.

StacCatalog.description: A static, file-based STAC catalogue (SUB-15). Holds one protection level (SEC-02).

debrief:schema_version.description: The newest data-file schema this catalogue holds (SUB-35).

StacCatalog.title: StacCatalog

StacItem.description: A STAC item. A plot is the item's "plot" asset (SUB-05, SUB-06).

items.description: [west, south, east, north] in WGS84 degrees.

StacItem.title: StacItem

created.description: When the item came into the catalogue (STAC common metadata): by import, as a received plot file, or as a copy. Items that came in after a plot can be new data for it (CAP-10).

datetime.description: Null when start_datetime and end_datetime are given.

debrief:coverage.description: The periods each of the item's tracks has data for (CAP-08), so a catalogue's coverage is read from its items alone. Derived at each change, never authoritative.

debrief:drawn_from.description: The catalogue items the plot's tracks take data from now, each at every revision a period of it was read at (CAP-12), from its tracks' supplies. Derived at each change, never authoritative.

debrief:imported.description: Whether the item came in by importing source files: its history starts with a record naming the files it read. Only such items can be new data for a plot (CAP-10; decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026). Derived at each change, never authoritative.

debrief:origin.description: The step_hash of the first step of the item's history: items that share it are copies of one plot, forked where their histories part (CAP-10). Derived at each change, never authoritative.

debrief:revision.description: The content hash of the item's plot, its whole-plot details included, so any recorded change to the item is a new revision (CAP-12). Derived at each change, never authoritative, as the extent is.

debrief:revisions.description: Every revision the item's history has had, each as the 16 symbols an image ID names it by (the first 80 bits of the content hash after each step, in Crockford's base 32), so an exported image is traced to its plot from the catalogue's items alone, never reading a plot that never had its revision (SUB-25). Derived at each change, never authoritative.

StacLink.description: Parent links are authoritative; child links are a hint only and are never trusted (SUB-23).
StacLink.title: StacLink

StepStateEnum.description: Where a step stands, as the after links and the current step say.
StepStateEnum.title: StepStateEnum

StoreKindEnum.description: How a store is reached. Only static file catalogues so far (SUB-15).
StoreKindEnum.title: StoreKindEnum

TimeRange.description: A closed interval of time. Start shall not be after end.
TimeRange.title: TimeRange

TimelineEntry.description: One row of the Timeline (CAP-05, CAP-20): a narrative entry, a time-only annotation (a note or a period) or a comment on a track's fix, as the Timeline lists them, in one time order.

colour.description: That track's colour, lower-case hex RGB.

end.description: The end of its period; left out for a single time.

entry_type.description: A narrative entry's type, in its source's words.

hidden.description: An annotation or track hidden on the map.

id.description: The narrative entry's or annotation's feature id, or fix:<track>:<time> for a fix's comment.

source.description: Who wrote a narrative entry; an annotation's name; the track a fix comment is on; the item supplying a period of data.

start.description: Its time, or the start of its period.

track.description: The track it belongs to: a narrative entry's track, or a fix's.

TimelineEntry.title: TimelineEntry

ToolDeclaration.description: How a tool describes itself to Debrief, agents and hooks (TL-04, TL-06).

applies_to.description: Feature kinds from the taxonomy, or "*" for any (TL-06). Debrief offers a tool only if every selected item matches (TL-08).

explanation.description: Short user-facing explanation of what the tool does (CAP-24).

judgement.description: Any judgement the tool involves, shown on its form (CAP-24).

name.description: Dotted, unique across loaded libraries, for example core.smooth_track.

uses_randomness.description: When true, Debrief records the seed (SUB-20).

ToolDeclaration.title: ToolDeclaration

ToolRef.description: The tool and version that performed an operation (SUB-24).
ToolRef.title: ToolRef

ToolResult.description: What a tool run returns (TL-11). Any combination of parts may be present.
ToolResult.title: ToolResult

ToteResult.description: The Tote at one time: the primary's own measures, and each secondary's measures relative to the primary and its own, as debrief/tote returns them and the Tote view shows them.

measures.description: The definitions of the group's measures, in its order.

note.description: What the analyst should know about the Tote as a whole, such as a measure group chosen that this plot's study does not have (core is shown instead).

rows.description: One per secondary, in the order chosen.

time.description: The time the values are for.

ToteResult.title: ToteResult

ToteRow.description: One track in the Tote at current time.

colour.description: The track's colour, lower-case hex, to key the row to the map.

note.description: Why there are no values, for the analyst, such as "Starts 09:30:00Z".

ToteRow.title: ToteRow

ToteRowStatusEnum.description: Whether a track in the Tote has values at current time.
ToteRowStatusEnum.title: ToteRowStatusEnum

ToteTrack.description: A track the analyst can put in the Tote, as the Tote view lists them.
ToteTrack.title: ToteTrack

ToteView.description: Which tracks the Tote compares, and through which measure group: view state in the plot's island, like the time window, so it travels with the plot file but is never a step in its history and never undone (SUB-22; decision, 14 Oct 2026). Ids of tracks no longer in the plot are shown as missing, not refused, because a change to content never changes the island.

map_lines.description: Whether the map draws a thin line from the primary to each secondary at current time; left out means it does (decision, 14 Oct 2026).

measure_group.description: The measure group shown; left out means core.

primary.description: The track the others are measured from; left out until one is chosen.

secondaries.description: The tracks measured from the primary, in the order shown.

ToteView.title: ToteView

TrackCoverage.description: The periods one track of an item has data for (CAP-05, CAP-08): from its first fix to its last, broken at each gap (a time between two fixes more than ten times the track's median time between fixes, and more than five minutes).
TrackCoverage.title: TrackCoverage

TrackEdit.description: A track moved, rotated, sheared or stretched by hand, as the map, a form or an agent describes it (CAP-01, CAP-02, CAP-21): one recorded, undoable step in the plot's history (SUB-19). Geodesic: a move takes every fix in the period the same range along the same bearing, each along its own geodesic; a rotation keeps each fix's range from the pivot and turns its bearing from the pivot by the angle. A shear and a stretch hold one end of the period (the anchor) and work in the azimuthal equidistant frame about it, where a geodesic through the anchor is a straight line: a shear adds to each fix the dragged end's displacement times the fix's fraction of the time from the anchor to the dragged end; a stretch scales each fix's range from the anchor, keeping its bearing from it. Either way a straight, steady leg stays a straight, steady leg. Fixes outside the period stay where they are, so the joins jump. A single fix moved (move_fix) goes where it is told, alone: its neighbours, its time and its recorded course and speed stay. set_plotting_mode with plotting_mode dr plots the whole track by dead reckoning, each fix placed from the one before by that fix's recorded course and speed, from the track's first fix; with otg it puts the fixes back where they were logged, after the analyst confirms losing any change made while plotted by dead reckoning (discard_dr_changes).

anchor.description: The end of the period a shear or a stretch holds fixed.

angle.description: How far a rotation turns the fixes about the pivot; positive is clockwise.

bearing.description: Which way a move takes each fix, a shear drags the end that is not held, or a single fix is moved, true, clockwise from north.

course.description: The course made good a shear gives the period: the true bearing, at its first fix, of the geodesic from its first fix to its last. With speed, instead of a distance and a bearing for the dragged end.

discard_dr_changes.description: set_plotting_mode to otg only: plot the track over the ground although it was changed while plotted by dead reckoning, losing those changes, as the analyst confirmed (decision, product owner, 14 Oct 2026). Without it such a change is refused, saying why.

distance.description: How far a move takes each fix, a shear drags the end that is not held, or a single fix is moved.

fix_time.description: The time of the one fix a move_fix moves: the fix is found by its time, as a mark is (where two fixes share a time, the first).

period.description: The fixes to change: those whose times fall in it, ends included. Left out, the whole track.

pivot.description: [longitude, latitude] of the position a rotation turns about. Left out, the fix nearest current time in the period, or the period's first fix.

plotting_mode.description: How set_plotting_mode plots the track, over the ground or by dead reckoning.

position.description: [longitude, latitude] a move_fix puts the fix at, instead of a distance and a bearing from where it is.

speed.description: The speed made good a shear or a stretch gives the period: the geodesic range from its first fix to its last over the time between.

TrackEdit.title: TrackEdit

TrackEditAnchorEnum.description: Which end of the period a shear or a stretch holds fixed; the other end is the one dragged.
TrackEditAnchorEnum.title: TrackEditAnchorEnum

TrackFeature.description: A platform track. Per-position values are parallel arrays matching the geometry.
TrackFeature.title: TrackFeature

TrackImportModeEnum.description: How tracks imported are plotted: ask for each track (the default), or one choice the analyst said to use for future imports. User state, kept here and never in a catalogue or a plot file.
TrackImportModeEnum.title: TrackImportModeEnum

arrow_interval.description: How often a chevron on the line shows the track's direction of travel (CAP-32): aligned and bounded as label_interval. Left out, Debrief's default: a few along the track in the time window.

courses.description: Course over ground at each position, true north, clockwise.

depths.description: Depth below the sea surface at each position, positive down. Absent where depth is not known.

fix_marks.description: Fixes with a colour, a label or a comment of their own, or always showing their time label or symbol, in time order, each found by its time (CAP-01, EXT-14). Most fixes have none, so only marked fixes are listed. Content: each change is a recorded, undoable step (SUB-22).

hidden.description: Not drawn on the map. Still listed, and still selectable, in the outline. Content: hiding is a recorded, undoable change (SUB-22).

label_interval.description: How often the track is labelled with the time (CAP-32): at each whole multiple of this interval of UTC (every 10 min is 0900, 0910, 0920...), as legacy Debrief aligns them, from 1 second to 24 hours; at every fix ("all"); or off. Left out, Debrief's default: none. Presentation content: each change is a recorded, undoable step, like colour (SUB-22).

logged_courses.description: A track plotted by dead reckoning: its courses as logged, one per fix, as they were when it was plotted so. On a DR track the courses and speeds are what edits change (decision, product owner, 14 Oct 2026), so these tell what was changed while plotted by dead reckoning, and plotting it over the ground again puts them back.

logged_positions.description: A track plotted by dead reckoning: its positions as logged, over the ground, one per fix, so plotting it over the ground again puts them back. Left out for a legacy plot's DR leg, which saved only the positions it worked out.

logged_speeds.description: A track plotted by dead reckoning: its speeds as logged, one per fix, as they were when it was plotted so; see logged_courses.

platform_links.description: Tracks in other catalogue items the analyst confirmed, or linked by hand, as this track's platform (CAP-09; decision, product owner, 16 Oct 2026). Tracks whose names match this one's, ignoring case and spaces, are proposed until confirmed or refused. Each change is a recorded, undoable step.

platform_unlinks.description: Tracks in other catalogue items whose names match this one's but which the analyst said are another platform: no longer proposed.

plotting_mode.description: How the track is plotted: over the ground (otg, as logged; also when left out) or by dead reckoning (dr), chosen as it was imported and changed as a recorded, undoable step (CAP-01, SUB-22). The geometry is always the positions as plotted, so other GeoJSON tools draw what Debrief draws.

speeds.description: Speed over ground at each position.

supplies.description: Which catalogue item supplies each period of the track (CAP-09): where two items have data for the platform over the same period, the analyst chooses which supplies it, and the track is stitched from the chosen periods. In time order, not overlapping, each from its first fix to its last. Left out, the plot itself supplies the whole track, as imported. Content: each change is a recorded, undoable step (SUB-22), naming the items and periods.

symbol_interval.description: How often a small symbol in the track's colour marks where it was (CAP-32): aligned and bounded as label_interval, or at every fix ("all"). Left out, none.

TrackStyle.description: How a track is drawn. Data colours do not change with the theme (DEV-07). Colour is content: the analyst changing it (blue friendly to red enemy, say) is a recorded, undoable change (SUB-22).

legacy_symbology.description: The REP symbology code the colour came from, such as "@C", kept for export.

TrackStyle.title: TrackStyle

TrackSupply.description: One period of a track and the catalogue item that supplies it (CAP-09): the fixes from start to end, ends included, are that item's track's (the plot's own, where it names the plot itself).

catalogue.description: The id in the item's catalog.json.

revision.description: The item's revision when the period was taken from it; left out where the plot supplies it itself.

title.description: The item's title when the period was taken from it.

track.description: The supplying track's feature id in that item.

TrackSupply.title: TrackSupply

config_version.description: Version of this file's layout: 1 while it holds only stores; 2 once it holds track_import_mode; 3 once it holds narrative_import. An earlier Debrief cannot read a later layout.

narrative_import.description: The analyst's last answers to the questions asked before a Word or PDF narrative is read into a plot, one set for each dialect, so they are offered again next time and confirmed with one key (CAP-19; product owner, 15 Oct 2026). User state, kept here and never in a catalogue or a plot file; importers are given the answers.

stores.description: Known stores, in the order the analyst sees them (SUB-17).

track_import_mode.description: How tracks imported are plotted, over the ground or by dead reckoning: ask (the default, also when left out), or otg or dr once the analyst chose "Use this choice for future imports" (CAP-01). The analyst may clear it, to be asked again.

items.description: [west, south, east, north] in WGS84 degrees, independent of display projection.

annotation.description: An annotation as the form describes it (show_annotation_form, save_annotation), as drawn on the map (annotation_drawn), or as changed on the map (edit_annotation).

context_tracks.description: How tracks outside the time window are drawn (CAP-29).

current_time.description: Current time from shared state, which a tool form offers for its time fields.

feature_id.description: The narrative entry the Timeline chose, changes or deletes, the annotation a form changes or deletes, the annotation or track the map asks to change, or the track whose fixes it rings or the analyst chose.

fix_time.description: The time of the fix the analyst chose on the map (fix_chosen).

fix_times.description: The times of the fixes the map rings (show_fixes).

hidden_count.description: How many of the plot's features are hidden on the map (SUB-22), so the map can say so.

image_request.description: What image to draw, and how (export_image).

item_revision.description: The item, at the revision the analyst saw (take_asked, dismiss_asked).

keep.description: Which of an ambiguous cut's bearings the analyst clicked, to keep (resolve_asked).

linked.description: Whether the source is the track's platform (link_changed).

minimum_context_contrast.description: The analyst's setting that shows faint context tracks as visible, so the time controller can say so.

narrative.description: A narrative entry as the Timeline's form describes it (save_narrative).

narrative_on_map.description: Whether the map shows the narrative entry current time is at beside its track (show_timeline, narrative_on_map_changed): the plot's PlotView.narrative_on_map; left out means it does.

plot_id.description: Which plot is open, as its host knows it (show_timeline): a list read again for the same plot keeps the reader's place; another plot is read from current time.

preview.description: A track as a change would leave it, one position per fix, drawn beside it until the analyst applies or cancels the change (show_fixes).

revision_shown.description: The plot shown is an earlier revision, read-only (show_plot).

saved_window.description: The time window as saved in the plot, so the time controller can say when the window shown differs from it (CAP-28).

source.description: A track in a catalogue item (source_chosen, link_changed).

time_range.description: The plot's period, so times can be entered as the analyst reads them (show_form) and the time window set within it (show_time); the time window to save (window_changed); or the period whose source the analyst chose (source_chosen).

timeline_entries.description: The Timeline's rows, in its order (show_timeline).

timeline_entry.description: The narrative entry current time is at, to show on the map beside its track (set_narrative).

timeline_tracks.description: The plot's tracks, which a narrative entry can belong to (show_timeline).

tote.description: The Tote's values at current time (show_tote).

tote_tracks.description: The plot's tracks, which the analyst can choose from for the Tote (show_tote).

tote_view.description: Which tracks the Tote compares, as saved in the plot (show_tote, set_tote) or as the analyst chose (tote_changed).

track_edit.description: How the analyst moved, rotated, sheared or stretched a track, or moved one of its fixes, on the map (edit_track).

description: The unit of analysis (SUB-05), stored as an asset of a STAC item.

history.description: The plot's whole history: every step, with its provenance and whether it is applied, undone or abandoned, and the current step (SUB-19, SUB-21, decision 13 Oct). A GeoJSON foreign member, so other tools still read the file as GeoJSON. Not content: left out of every content hash. Last in the file. A plot sent to a view or a tool never carries it.

title: debrief
